newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Son of Bulgarian king to advise President.
newsitem.headline: Son of Bulgarian king to advise President.

text.p: Prince Kiril, son of Bulgaria's exiled King Simeon II, arrived on Tuesday in Sofia to advise President Petar Stoyanov on stabilising the economy.

Simeon's second son, Kiril Saxe-Coburg-Gotha, an economist at London-based investment bank Lehman Brothers International, was met at the airport by a small group of royalists with flowers and the traditional Bulgarian welcome gifts of bread and salt.
Prince Kiril said he expected during his two-day visit to Sofia to discuss and exchange views on the economic situation in Bulgaria.
"At this moment we are mainly going to review what are their options and then discuss and see what is best for the country," Prince Kiril told Reuters on arrival at the airport.

"I think that I will express the opinion of the international financial community that the introduction of a currency board in Bulgaria is an extremely positive step and we will discuss the measures related to this board," he said.
Bulgaria's new reformist government, elected last month, is due to launch on July 1 a restrictive monetary system known as currency board.

Simeon, who lives in Madrid and works as a business consultant, fled Bulgaria as a child in 1946 after the Soviet Red Army installed a puppet communist regime. He has two other sons ,Kardam and Kubrat, and a daughter Kalina.
King Simeon II came home for the first time after 50 years of exile last year and visited Bulgaria again in April before the country's general elections, won by the Union of Democratic Forces.
Later on Tuesday Prince Kiril will meet President Stoyanov and will attend a meeting of the President's Economic Development Council.
He is due to meet on Wednesday Prime Minister Ivan Kostov, the Privatisation Agency executive director Alexander Sabotinov and the Deputy Prime Minister and Industry Minister Alexander Bozhkov.
